## Summary

The vulnerability was in `PostController.update` (`app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts`): it read the raw request body with `this.request.json()` and passed it straight to `Post.forceUpdate`, which bypasses both validation and the model's mass-assignment allowlist (`Post.fillable = ['title', 'excerpt', 'body']`). This let any field — including `authorId` or `createdAt` — flow straight into the row, and skipped the required/length checks that `store` already applies.

The fix makes `update` mirror `store`: it now validates the body against the existing `PostPayloadSchema` (`title`/`excerpt`/`body`, same required/length rules used at creation) and writes through `Post.update` instead of `Post.forceUpdate`, so only fillable columns are ever persisted — `authorId` can no longer be set from request input under any circumstances, invalid edits are rejected with a 422 and field errors without touching the row, and non-author edits still 403 as before.

Added `tests/PostControllerUpdate.test.ts` with feature tests (using `TestApp`, real SQLite via `resetDatabase()`) covering: the author-reassignment attack is blocked, extraneous fields like `createdAt` are dropped, an empty title is rejected with 422 and leaves the post unchanged, valid author edits still work, and non-authors still get 403. `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` both pass (7/7 tests, including the two pre-existing ones).
